circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometer track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has hosted Formula One's season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second Middle Eastern circuit to join the F1 calendar, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit located around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this track hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year along with supporting motorsport events. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification for its facilities and infrastructure.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Situated in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, it was renamed and returned to hosting the championship race from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, inaugurated in 2004, is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and endurance events, with multiple circuit configurations available for different series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the 4. 657 km Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya features a diverse layout combining extended straights with varied corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all-around racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near Stavelot in Belgium's Wallonia region, Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit that has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, including races during the inaugural 1950 Formula One season. The venue has maintained annual Grand Prix status since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its primary role as an F1 venue, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track also began staging the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English racing facility has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. It gained historic significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the event moved between three venues until becoming a permanent fixture here in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the track also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix ever held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city after government preference overruled plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (except for 1980 during renovations), earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" through its characteristic long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is renowned for hosting prestigious Formula One races alongside Japanese Super Formula championship events.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding streets lined with major hotels and casinos. The layout passes iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of the most visually distinctive racing venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two racing brothers who tragically died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, featuring a revised track layout compared to its earlier configurations that last saw F1 competition in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary 3. 363-mile circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, featuring 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track debuted on the championship calendar in 2022 and has since become the primary venue for the Miami Grand Prix, while also hosting electric racing series from 2025-26 onward.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around Monaco's harbor. Though officially known by its full name, it is widely called "Monte Carlo" since most of the track runs through that district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix beginning in 2021 after a lengthy absence from the Formula One calendar. The venue's Formula One tenure concluded following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, this 4. 309 km Brazilian circuit opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The anticlockwise track hosts major racing events and features a companion kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Red Sea coastline in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, which has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural year in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the urban areas of Downtown Core and Kallang as it traces a path around the bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Catalonia, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and technical corners that test all aspects of driver skill. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility hosting multiple racing series, most notably the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue regularly accommodates NASCAR, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the FIA World Endurance Championship's Lone Star Le Mans event, along with various other motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai-British racing driver who currently competes for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, is a two-time world champion having claimed titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and securing two Le Mans victories with Toyota, making him uniquely the only driver to claim both a Formula One world championship and a world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes on the Formula One grid in 2025 and has secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career with the team.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian driver, races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the sport. He has achieved two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during his time with Mercedes and has claimed victory in ten Grand Prix events throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One for Alpine, representing his country in the sport's top tier.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver who races in European Le Mans Series prototypes while holding a reserve position with Haas in Formula One, having made appearances at seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding the joint-record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his lengthy career in the sport. Beyond single-seaters, he achieved major success in endurance racing, most notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One racing for Ferrari, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories over his nine-season career. He narrowly missed out on the world championship in 2022, finishing as runner-up that year.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who returned to Formula One for the 2022 season after a two-year absence, competing through 2024. Currently, he focuses on sports car racing with BMW in the World Endurance Championship while maintaining a part-time presence in NASCAR.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025. Across his eight-season career, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The talented competitor secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The veteran competitor achieved second place in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-season career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport over four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in the IMSA series.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently drives for Aston Martin in Formula One racing.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda competed as a full-time Formula One participant between 2021 and 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for the 2026 season, supporting both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Championships between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing. The driver has accumulated 72 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine F1 since 2021, adopting the name of Renault's sports car brand following its previous identity as Renault F1 Team. Operating as Renault's factory team throughout this period, Alpine maintained this works status until Renault's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, the British automotive manufacturer, has maintained an intermittent presence in Formula One through different corporate structures, with its current iteration competing under the AMR GP Limited banner as a works team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the championship since its inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially identified by its emblematic horse symbol, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad entered the sport in 2016 and has been helmed by Ayao Komatsu since early 2024, following the departure of long-serving principal Guenther Steiner who oversaw the team from its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss motorsport engineering company founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber that achieved notable success in endurance racing, including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours. After joining Formula One in 1993, the independent constructor competed for over three decades before ceasing operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving teams. Audi acquired the organization in 2024 to establish its own Formula One team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group. The team, now sponsored by Mastercard in its F1 designation, is wholly owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both team ownership and engine supply. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, operates from Brackley under a German licence with ownership shared between Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff as of 2022. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams under Red Bull ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team within the Red Bull Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team based in Faenza that began competing in 2024 as one of two constructors under Red Bull ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. The team maintains operations in both Italy and Milton Keynes, where it works in proximity to its sister outfit.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team established in 2005 and based in England, owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside sister team Racing Bulls. Under Christian Horner's management from its inception through 2024, the team became a dominant force in the sport, though Horner departed in 2025 and was succeeded by Laurent Mekies as team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerged from the ashes of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant force in the sport's history, competing under various title sponsorships including Atlassian in 2026.
